quests.instruction: Some families eat dinner at five o'clock and others eat at eight. What does this show about dinner time?
quests.correctAnswer: It can vary from family to family
options: It must be exactly the same everywhere
It can vary from family to family
quests.explanation: Dinner is usually in the evening, but the exact time changes with schedules, cultures, and seasons.
quests.funFact: In some countries families eat dinner very late in the evening.

quests.instruction: Mia says, "The Moon only comes out at night." What is a more accurate thing to say?
quests.correctAnswer: Often at night, but sometimes in daytime too
options: It is never in the sky during the day
Often at night, but sometimes in daytime too
quests.hint: Look for the answer that leaves room for what you have seen.
quests.explanation: The Moon is above the horizon for part of every day, so it can be seen in the daytime when it is bright enough.
quests.funFact: A Moon in the daytime sky is very common near the first and last quarter phases.

quests.instruction: A nurse works through the night in a hospital and sleeps in the morning. What can we say about her sleep?
quests.correctAnswer: People can sleep at different times
options: Nobody can sleep during the day
People can sleep at different times
quests.explanation: Many people, like nurses and bakers, work at times that are not typical, so they may sleep during the day.
quests.funFact: Some jobs, like firefighting and hospital care, need people around the clock.

quests.instruction: Which sentence about children and play is the most accurate?
quests.correctAnswer: Children usually play outside in the daytime
options: Children usually play outside in the daytime
Children can only play outside in the daytime
quests.hint: Watch for the word that makes a rule too strict.
quests.explanation: Children usually play outside in the daytime, but on summer evenings or at night events they sometimes do too.
quests.funFact: The word usually leaves room for exceptions.

quests.instruction: In the far north in summer, the Sun can stay up almost all day and night. What does this show?
quests.correctAnswer: Day length can change with place and season
options: Day length can change with place and season
Day length is always the same
quests.explanation: Near the poles, the Sun can stay above the horizon for many hours in summer, so day and night lengths change.
quests.funFact: Parts of northern Norway have a midnight Sun in summer.

quests.instruction: Which is more accurate: "We always have dinner at night" or "Many families have dinner in the evening"?
quests.correctAnswer: Many families have dinner in the evening
options: Many families have dinner in the evening
We always have dinner at night
quests.hint: Look for the most careful wording.
quests.explanation: Not everyone eats dinner at the same time, so the careful statement is that many families do in the evening.
quests.funFact: In Spain, many people eat dinner after nine o'clock, which is later than in many other countries.

quests.instruction: Winter days in many places are shorter than summer days. What does this mean for the Sun?
quests.correctAnswer: It sets earlier in winter
options: It never sets in winter
It sets earlier in winter
quests.explanation: Winter days have fewer hours of daylight in many places, so the Sun sets earlier.
quests.funFact: The shortest day of the year is in December in the northern half of the world.

quests.instruction: A bakery opens before sunrise. Does this mean bakeries are always open at night?
quests.correctAnswer: No, some open early and close in the day
options: No, some open early and close in the day
Yes, every bakery is open all night
quests.hint: One example does not make a rule.
quests.explanation: Opening hours vary, and a bakery opening before sunrise does not mean they all stay open all night.
quests.funFact: Many bakeries start work in the small hours.

quests.instruction: Which of these changes from person to person?
quests.correctAnswer: The time they wake up
options: The time they wake up
The number of hours in a day
quests.hint: One of these is the same for everyone. The other depends on schedules.
quests.explanation: People wake up at different times depending on school, work, and habits. A day has the same number of hours for everyone.
quests.funFact: Early risers and night owls are real habits.

quests.instruction: Can you sometimes still see a few bright stars just before sunrise?
quests.correctAnswer: Yes, a few bright ones
options: Yes, a few bright ones
No, never at all
quests.explanation: Before the sky is fully bright, a few of the brightest stars and planets can still be seen. As sunlight grows, they fade from view.
quests.funFact: The planet Venus is sometimes called the morning star.

quests.instruction: At the start of summer, which statement is accurate for many places?
quests.correctAnswer: Days are longer than nights
options: Days are shorter than nights
Days are longer than nights
quests.explanation: In summer in many places, there are more hours of daylight than darkness.
quests.funFact: The longest day of the year happens in summer.

quests.instruction: If your friend plays outside at 8 p.m., does that mean it is not night?
quests.correctAnswer: It depends on the season and place
options: It depends on the season and place
Yes, 8 p.m. is always daytime
quests.explanation: In some places and seasons it is still light at 8 p.m., and in others it is dark.
quests.funFact: In summer, evenings can stay light late in the north.

quests.instruction: Some animals, like deer, are active at dawn and dusk. What does that mean?
quests.correctAnswer: Not all animals are only day or night
options: All animals are either day or night only
Not all animals are only day or night
quests.hint: Pay attention to the in-between times.
quests.explanation: Crepuscular animals are most active at twilight, in between day and night.
quests.funFact: Rabbits have long ears that can turn to catch faint sounds.

quests.instruction: Which sentence is true?
quests.correctAnswer: Many go to bed in the evening, at different times
options: All children go to bed at 7 p.m.
Many go to bed in the evening, at different times
quests.explanation: Bedtimes differ because ages, families, and schedules differ.
quests.funFact: Newborn babies sleep many hours in short stretches, and the stretches get longer as they grow.

quests.instruction: Does the Sun set at exactly the same time every day?
quests.correctAnswer: No, it changes through the year
options: No, it changes through the year
Yes, it never changes
quests.explanation: Sunset time shifts through the year as seasons change.
quests.funFact: Sunset can be hours earlier in winter than in summer.

quests.instruction: A school starts at eight in one country and at noon in another. Which is true?
quests.correctAnswer: School start times differ
options: School start times differ
School always starts in the morning
quests.explanation: Schools can start at different times in different places.
quests.funFact: Some schools have shifts for morning and afternoon classes.

quests.instruction: Can an owl be active in the daytime?
quests.correctAnswer: Some kinds can
options: No owl ever is
Some kinds can
quests.explanation: Most owls are nocturnal, but some, like the snowy owl, can hunt in daylight.
quests.funFact: Burrowing owls are also often active in daylight.

quests.instruction: Which sentence about animals leaves room for exceptions?
quests.correctAnswer: Many animals favor one part of the day
options: Many animals favor one part of the day
All animals sleep at the same time
quests.explanation: Different animals have different activity patterns.
quests.funFact: Cats often sleep somewhere between twelve and sixteen hours a day.

quests.instruction: It is noon, yet the sky is very dark during a storm. What is the explanation?
quests.correctAnswer: Thick storm clouds block sunlight
options: Night came early
Thick storm clouds block sunlight
quests.hint: It is the middle of the day.
quests.explanation: Heavy clouds can block much of the sunlight and make daytime dim.
quests.funFact: Storm clouds can be tall and thick.

quests.instruction: Which of these do people do at different times in different places?
quests.correctAnswer: Eat lunch
options: Look at the Sun
Eat lunch
quests.explanation: Lunch time changes depending on culture.
quests.funFact: In some countries lunch is the largest meal.

quests.instruction: Does dawn happen at the same time for everyone on Earth?
quests.correctAnswer: No, it moves around the Earth
options: Yes, at the same moment
No, it moves around the Earth
quests.explanation: Dawn arrives at different times in different places as the Earth turns.
quests.funFact: Time zones were invented because of this.

quests.instruction: Your friend says, "Shadows are always long in the morning." What should you say?
quests.correctAnswer: Often, but they shrink as the Sun climbs
options: Often, but they shrink as the Sun climbs
Always, all day long
quests.hint: Focus on shadows through the morning.
quests.explanation: Shadows are long near sunrise and shrink as the Sun rises.
quests.funFact: A shadow's tip creeps along the ground as the Sun's position changes during the day.

quests.instruction: A child in a very cloudy place says, "I have not seen the Sun for three days." Does that mean it was night?
quests.correctAnswer: No, clouds hid the Sun
options: No, clouds hid the Sun
Yes, it was night
quests.explanation: Clouds can hide the Sun for days, but day still happens.
quests.funFact: Clouds can cover large parts of the sky.

quests.instruction: People may have breakfast at different times. Which is a good general statement?
quests.correctAnswer: Breakfast usually happens after waking up
options: Breakfast usually happens after waking up
Breakfast only happens at 7 a.m.
quests.explanation: Breakfast follows waking up, whatever the clock says.
quests.funFact: Some people have a late breakfast called brunch.

quests.instruction: The Sun is up during daytime. Can the Sun also be seen at night anywhere on Earth?
quests.correctAnswer: In some far-north places in summer
options: Never, not anywhere on Earth
In some far-north places in summer
quests.explanation: Near the poles in summer, the Sun can be seen at midnight.
quests.funFact: In Tromso, Norway, the Sun stays above the horizon for weeks in summer.

quests.instruction: Which is best: "It is always dark at 6 p.m." or "It depends on the season and place"?
quests.correctAnswer: It depends on the season and place
options: It depends on the season and place
It is always dark at 6 p.m.
quests.explanation: Sunset time depends on place and season.
quests.funFact: Many places have light at 6 p.m. in summer.

quests.instruction: Which sentence is the most accurate?
quests.correctAnswer: Night is usually best for seeing stars
options: Night is usually best for seeing stars
Stars only exist at night
quests.explanation: Stars are always there, but we see them best in the dark.
quests.funFact: Stars are in the sky during the day too.

quests.instruction: Bears sleep a lot in winter. Is this the same as sleeping at night?
quests.correctAnswer: No, it is a long winter rest
options: Yes, it is exactly the same
No, it is a long winter rest
quests.explanation: Some bears have a long winter rest, different from a night's sleep.
quests.funFact: Bears can wake up during their winter rest.

quests.instruction: A week-long camping trip: the group sees the Moon rise at different times each night. What does that show?
quests.correctAnswer: Moonrise time changes from day to day
options: The Moon rises at the same time every day
Moonrise time changes from day to day
quests.explanation: The Moon rises about 50 minutes later each day on average.
quests.funFact: This is because the Moon moves around Earth.

quests.instruction: When people say "daytime", what do they usually mean?
quests.correctAnswer: The time when it is light outside
options: The time from midnight to noon
The time when it is light outside
quests.explanation: Daytime usually means when the Sun is up and it is light.
quests.funFact: Daytime lasts different lengths depending on the season.
